findings.summary: FakeEnvironment does not enforce the contract's decided postcondition that GetBaseDirectory() 'reproduces a separator-terminated value' (Decision 5) — it echoes back whatever string the caller supplies, so the interface's own documented guarantee has no owner enforcing it in the fake.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs:85 (`baseDirectory ?? home,` — the default fallback stores `home` verbatim with no separator normalization) and :108 (`public string GetBaseDirectory() => _baseDirectory;` — a bare pass-through of whatever was stored). The interface itself states the postcondition at src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts/IEnvironment.cs:52 ('terminated with a directory separator'), which FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() inherits via `<inheritdoc />` but does not fulfill. Not hypothetical: the default construction path every test uses, SystemServicesBuilder.Fake().Build() at tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/SystemServicesBuilder.cs:247-251, calls `FakeEnvironment.Create(Host.Home, tempDirectory: Host.Temp, ...)` with no `baseDirectory:` argument, so GetBaseDirectory() falls back to Host.Home — sourced (SystemServicesBuilder.cs:294-304) from the real EnvironmentAdapter.GetHomeDirectory() (`Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.UserProfile)`), a value that is never separator-terminated on macOS, Linux, or Windows. So on the real host today, SystemServicesBuilder.Fake().Build().Environment.GetBaseDirectory() already returns a non-separator-terminated string, contradicting both the interface's documented guarantee and Decision 5's explicit requirement. GetHomeDirectory() carries no such documented postcondition (no separator language on it in IEnvironment.cs), so this is not excused by the existing pass-through pattern used for home/current/temp — GetBaseDirectory() is the one member the contract singled out for faithful mirroring, and the shape doesn't deliver it.

refutationAttempts: Checked whether this is out-of-scope 'missing behavior' since architecture bodies are meant to throw NotImplementedException — refuted: FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory() is not a stub, it is fully implemented data storage exactly like its GetHomeDirectory/GetCurrentDirectory/GetTempDirectory siblings, so its behavioral fidelity to the contract is in scope for this lens.

Checked whether the existing '?? home' pass-through pattern used for currentDirectory/tempDirectory excuses the same pattern here — refuted: those members carry no documented separator postcondition in IEnvironment.cs, while GetBaseDirectory() is the one member the contract (Decision 5) explicitly requires to mirror AppContext.BaseDirectory's separator-terminated guarantee.

Verified the violation is live today, not merely a future risk, by tracing SystemServicesBuilder.Fake()'s default Build() path (SystemServicesBuilder.cs:245-252) through Host.Home (sourced from the real EnvironmentAdapter.GetHomeDirectory(), SystemServicesBuilder.cs:294-304) to confirm the default fake environment used across the whole test suite already returns a non-separator-terminated base directory.

Re-read Decision 5's closing clause 'Tim may still choose to normalize instead' to check whether it retracts the requirement — it does not; it reads as a forward-looking option on a different question (whether the real adapter should normalize away the OS-provided separator), not a retraction of 'the fake reproduces a separator-terminated value' as the decision taken now.

Checked the three required surfaces (IEnvironment, EnvironmentAdapter, FakeEnvironment) for placement/assembly/signature fidelity to Decisions 2 and the Surfaces section — all three agree on the member name, signature, and assembly placement, so no separate finding there.
